A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimWorld-Robotics work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, Appendices A-G, and the checklist. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments on SimWorld-MMNav and SimWorld-MRS in Tables 2-5, plus runtime measurements, ablations, and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments, runtime measurements, ablations, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A, C, and D retain the same simulator components, agent controls, task-generation algorithms, finetuning objectives, and inference pipelines.

E1.justification: Both versions use SimWorld-20K training data, SimWorld-MMNav easy and hard navigation scenarios, and SimWorld-MRS collaborative search. No dataset, task, or evaluated environment coverage changes.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 retain the same evaluated VLMs, finetuned model, HybridGPT, VLA-RL, and oracle/RoCo comparisons. Bibliographic corrections do not change comparator participation.

E3.justification: Reported data splits, task counts, input modalities, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged in Sections 4.1 and 5.1 and Appendices C-D.

E4.justification: The failure analysis in Table 4, component ablations in Table 11, runtime stress tests in Appendix A.11, and qualitative cases in Appendix E are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both retain the 95% confidence-interval reporting and binomial interval method in Appendix C.6/Table 12. The checklist statement that each experiment was run twice is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results in Tables 2-5, 7, 11-12 and Appendix E match. For example, finetuned QwenVL 2.5 7B retains 4.0% success and 52.45% subtask success on the easy task set.

T1.justification: The task specifications and metric definitions in Equations (1)-(3) are unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same simulator, benchmark, and training-dataset contributions and claims about existing models' limitations and benefits of finetuning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of grounding, spatial reasoning, communication failures, and finetuning limitations remain unchanged. Both retain the outdoor-only scope and limited human-action repertoire discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, prompts, Table 10 hyperparameters, hardware information, and the project link are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same deferred code-release statement.

R1.justification: DriVLMe, RobotSlang, and SimWorld were already cited in v1; v2 revises their bibliographic metadata. The cited-work coverage, related-work discussion, and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 replaces DriVLMe and RobotSlang placeholder references with named authors and revised titles and dates, updates the SimWorld entry, removes bibliography URLs/DOIs, and renumbers citations. Main prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened and reordered bibliography reflows across pages 11-15. Scientific figures, table structures, algorithms, and appendix placement remain unchanged apart from citation-label updates.

improvement.justification: Replacing the two 'Firstname Lastname and Others' references with named authors and specific titles improves attribution and source identification. The SimWorld entry also gains fuller identification. Removing bibliography URLs/DOIs reduces lookup convenience, but resolving the unfinished references provides a limited net benefit; scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged.
